title: The Principles of Communism
author: Friedrich Engels
shortDescription: Drafted by Friedrich Engels in 1847 as a 25-question catechism for the Communist League, this foundational work provides clear, accessible answers explaining the core principles of Marxism.
subject: Classical Marxism
context: Written in October to November 1847 as a draft program for the Communist League in Paris, 'The Principles of Communism' uses a simple question-and-answer format to explain the origins of the proletariat, the nature of industrial capitalism, and the necessity of socialist revolution. It served as the immediate structural foundation for Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels when writing 'The Communist Manifesto' a few months later.
relatesToToday: Provides a straightforward Q&A guide to economic inequality today. It explains why automation and AI threaten job security under private ownership, but could drastically shorten the workweek and guarantee universal housing and healthcare if technology were run for public benefit.
keyTakeaways: The proletariat is the modern working class created by the Industrial Revolution, living entirely by selling its labor-power under market competition.
Machine production constantly increases output capacity, leading to periodic crises of overproduction under capitalist private property.
Private property has become an obstacle to social development; communism replaces market anarchy with democratic, planned social production.
Proletarian revolution requires international coordination across industrial nations and progressive social measures (public education, taxation, socialized industry).
